title: Refurbishing a Tektronix TDS7104 Oscilloscope: A Detailed Restoration Guide
summary: A comprehensive guide detailing the step-by-step process of refurbishing a Tektronix TDS7104 oscilloscope, including common failures, hardware disassembly, hard drive imaging, battery replacement, OS reinstallation challenges, and component-specific troubleshooting.
key_points: The Tektronix TDS7104 is a high-performance 1 GHz bandwidth oscilloscope with historical significance, originally running Windows 2000 Pro Embedded.
Common failures include dead CMOS/PowerPC backup batteries, failing hard drives, and power supply capacitor leaks.
Initial steps should always include imaging the hard drive (e.g., using HDD Raw Copy Tool) to preserve data before attempting repairs.
Replacing the CR2032 backup battery may require adjusting display settings (e.g., True Color 24-bit mode) to resolve graphical corruption.
Disassembly requires removing over 30 screws (Torx-15) and careful handling of the front panel to avoid breaking plastic tabs.
Attempts to upgrade to an SSD may fail due to compatibility issues with older systems, necessitating a fresh OS installation.
Reinstalling Windows 2000 Pro involves challenges like non-functional CD-ROM drives, BIOS limitations (e.g., no USB boot), and driver compatibility.
TEAC CD-224E drives vary by version (e.g., A93 vs. CD0), and not all are compatible with the TDS7104 motherboard.
Workarounds for installation include using a virtual machine or bootable USB sticks with tools like WinSetupFromUSB and Plop Boot Manager.
Specialized drivers (e.g., Tektronix firmware, TekFonts) and license keys are required to fully restore functionality.
